title: Finance Payroll Average
body:
Write one SQL query that returns the average salary of the Finance department of the company named Acme Corp. Join the three tables, filter on both names, group by company name and department name, and do not round the average.

Return the columns company_name, department_name, average_salary, in that order. If Acme Corp has no Finance department with employees, the result is empty. Rows may be in any order.
inp: The three tables below. Each test runs your query on a different set of rows.
out: The rows of your query, compared as a set. Averages are compared to within 0.001.
cons: Name matches are exact and case-sensitive
A company can have more than one department with the same name

samples.ex: Departments 100 belongs to Acme Corp Finance: (90000 + 75500 + 81000) / 3 = 82166.666…

ref:
SELECT c.company_name, d.department_name, AVG(e.salary) AS average_salary
FROM employees e
JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.department_id
JOIN companies c ON d.company_id = c.company_id
WHERE c.company_name = 'Acme Corp' AND d.department_name = 'Finance'
GROUP BY c.company_name, d.department_name;
